URL: https://www.chathamhouse.org/2026/05/trump-xi-summit-can-progress-be-made-iran

Chatham House analysis on Trump-Xi summit and Iran:

Key framing:
- "the standoff in the Strait of Hormuz and the state of AI have been developing so fast" — limited US-side clarity on summit goals
- Both powers have an interest in opening the Strait of Hormuz and making progress on AI safety
- China has "some leverage with Iran but will want something from the US in return, if it is to use it"

Wang Yi statement:
- China's top diplomat called for the Strait of Hormuz to be opened "as soon as possible" in talks with his Iranian counterpart
- Wang Yi met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Beijing

Context:
- Asian countries including China have been among the most affected by interruption to supplies of oil, gas, fertiliser and helium (needed for semiconductors, healthcare and pharmaceuticals)
- US list of concrete deliverables is short: keep rare earths flowing, create a board of trade mechanism, secure Chinese purchase commitments
- "gap between this short agenda and the long list of issues between two nations engaged in grinding, multidimensional competition reveals a shared preference for managing their rivalry rather than resolving it"
